A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Renamed methods and relocated analyses can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments comparing supervised fine-tuning, SSL, and ensemble self-training, together with scalability, initialization, and hyperparameter-tuning analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds classifier-head comparisons, prediction-overlap measurements, and an ablation involving unequal-quality pseudo-label sources.

M1.justification: ST(PEFT) and ST(PEFT+VFMs) are renamed PET and V-PET. Algorithm 1 restates v1 Section 5.4: supervised PEFT, one-hot pseudo-label generation and averaging, followed by single-round self-training. No actual procedural change is established.

E1.justification: Documented coverage retains DTD, SUN397, Resisc45, Retinopathy, Clevr-C, and KITTI, alongside the CIFAR-10/100 and Food101 probing comparisons. The added analyses concern classifier heads and pseudo-label sources; segmentation and detection are mentioned only as future directions.

E2.justification: v2 Table 8 adds frozen-backbone MLP-96 and MLP-768 comparisons alongside linear heads and LoRA. The main SSL comparator set remains FixMatch, FlexMatch, SoftMatch, FineSSL, labeled-only training, and ordinary self-training.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce MLP widths of 96/768, a top-20%-confidence subset, and controlled pseudo-label-source comparisons. Table 2 also changes Retinopathy labels per class from 40/80 to 4/8 and Clevr-C from 10/20 to 1/2, contradicting v2's retained result-table settings. This establishes a reporting change, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds confidence-overlap analysis in Figure 1, classifier-head capacity controls in Appendix B.4/Table 8, and unequal-quality teacher ensembling in Appendix B.6/Table 10. These extend the existing analyses; scalability, aggregation-strategy, initialization, and tuning studies remain, including material moved into the appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs with randomly sampled pseudo-label-source sets for scalability and retain the corresponding error-bar plots. Mean and standard deviation reporting for tuning errors is unchanged between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 11. The added analyses introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Table 3 and the matched detailed baseline, PEFT, and tuning tables retain their numerical values. v2 adds MLP-head accuracies, confidence-overlap counts, and Table 10 results of 56.17%, 25.27%, and 58.62% for training CLIP-B with CLIP, ViT-B-IN21k, and combined pseudo-label sources. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The classification formulation, pseudo-label averaging, validator definitions, and rank-aggregation mathematics in Appendix C are substantively unchanged. Algorithm 1 reformats existing mathematics; neither version adds a theoretical guarantee or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that labeled-only PEFT is competitive with existing SSL and that ensembling predictions across PEFT methods and VFMs provides an effective self-training baseline. The revised abstract and PET/V-PET terminology retain these central contributions rather than establish new core claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly identifies classification as the demonstrated scope and treats segmentation/detection as prospective extensions. Section 6.2 and Appendix B.6 additionally argue that ensembling can remain beneficial when pseudo-label sources differ substantially in quality, extending the earlier emphasis on similarly performant, complementary learners.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the new MLP heads as single-hidden-layer networks with widths 96/768. However, it omits v1 Section 5.4's explicit KL-divergence training-loss specification. Hardware, hyperparameter search spaces, and code-access information remain unchanged; the new Table 10 experiment lacks an identified dataset and shot setting.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused transfer-learning and self-supervised-learning discussion, PEFT/transfer surveys, and CLIP pseudo-labeling studies by Menghini et al. and Zhang et al. It elaborates distinctions from FineSSL and methods requiring CLIP's zero-shot capabilities while retaining the original VFM-specific research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial portions of the introduction, and benchmark motivation are rewritten. Method subsections are consolidated, the ST variants receive PET/V-PET names, and staged algorithm prose becomes pseudocode. Experimental discussion is reorganized, with v1 Sections 6.4–6.5 moved into Appendix B.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. The pipeline is redrawn as Figure 2; new Figure 1 combines a Venn diagram with a line-chart rendering of the earlier ensemble comparison. Algorithm 1 and Tables 8 and 10 are added.

improvement.justification: The new classifier-head controls, direct diversity evidence, and expanded related work strengthen support and exposition. However, v2 introduces conflicting label budgets in Table 2, removes the explicit KL-loss specification, and leaves the new weak-source experiment's dataset/shot setting unspecified. With the principal results unchanged, these evidential gains and reproducibility regressions do not establish a clear net quality improvement.
